note: The bands Extreme Flight's 105.5 in Slick 580 plant has to land in, from docs/SLICK-STAGE1.md, which derives each from EF's data sheet and drawing, Desert Aircraft's DA-120, Falcon's measured static table for the DA-120 on its 28 x 10 and APC's data for the prop's shape (npm run slick:derive prints them; --check holds these derived figures to it). The widths are the Extra's (tests/extra-thresholds.json), each for the same reason. Never widened to pass; argue in the derivation instead.

s1_level_75.source: level speed at 75 percent of the throttle stick, the engine floating on its map against APC's 28 x 10 curves (at this speed it reaches DA's 6,900 rpm cap, as at full), derived 41.70 from Falcon's thrust, the curves and the component drag build up; 12 percent either way, the Extra's, for the thrust line's slope and cd0

s2_stall.source: sqrt(2W / rho S CLmax) at the wing's CLmax at the stall's own Reynolds number, 4.4e5 on the mean chord: 0.902, 0.9 of Sheldahl and Klimas' NACA 0012 (SAND80-2114 Table 2: 0.9811 at 3.6e5, 1.0749 at 7e5), derived 13.88; alphaStall CLmax over the wing's own slope; the Extra's band in proportion, 0.94 to 1.14 of the formula, since the plant reads the stall at the blend's midpoint

s3_glide.source: L/D at 1.4 Vs, 19.4 m/s, derived 14.06, 12 percent either way, the Extra's

s4_top.source: level speed at full throttle, the engine at DA's 6,900 rpm cap (engine_rpm_max) on APC's 28 x 10 curves, derived 41.70, 10 percent either way

s5_roll.source: pb/2V at full aileron on the sheet's high rate (38 up, 37 down), Clda throw_a / -Clp, derived 0.3696 (348 deg/s at 22 m/s); 25 percent either way, the width the large deflection correction K' carries. EF's 'blistering roll rate'

s6_hover.source: hanging on the prop, the nose held up by the elevator and rudder in the slipstream, the height by the throttle: the rpm share where the thrust meets the weight, sqrt(W / T cos 3 deg) 0.6348, as the stick that holds it standing on the DA-120's map (engine_q), derived 0.3736; 5 percent either way

s7_vertical.source: straight up at full throttle, the climb speed where the thrust, the engine floating on its map against APC's curves, meets the weight and the zero lift drag, derived 30.03; 10 percent either way

s8_torque_roll.source: hanging at the hover with the ailerons let go: the prop's torque_arm W less the swirl's roll (SWIRL_KEEP 0.65, Selig 2010, docs/FLIGHTMODEL.md) and less the roll of the fin holding the right thrust's yaw (thrust_yaw 3 deg, prop_x T sin 3 deg over l_v at the fin's height z_v), against the air the turning wing sweeps through (rot_k), steady at sqrt(Q / k), derived 125 deg/s, to the left; 25 percent either way. The fin meets the swirl the static jet brings it, slip_loss[2] (Deters, Ananda and Selig 2015, AIAA 2015-2265, figs. 15a and 15b; ~/Desktop/fdfpv-loop/research/wash-speed/WASH-SPEED.md), and SWIRL_KEEP holds Selig's 0.40 at 0.65 (was 0.74); was 136, the band 102 to 170.

s9_aileron_hover.source: the same with full right aileron: the ailerons' inboard share in the slipstream beats the net torque, derived 149 deg/s right; 40 percent either way, the difference of two estimates. The fin meets the swirl the static jet brings it, slip_loss[2] (Deters, Ananda and Selig 2015, AIAA 2015-2265, figs. 15a and 15b; ~/Desktop/fdfpv-loop/research/wash-speed/WASH-SPEED.md), and SWIRL_KEEP holds Selig's 0.40 at 0.65 (was 0.74); was 139.3, the band 84 to 195.

s10_zero_speed.source: hanging still, full up elevator and full right rudder from rest: the slipstream's dp on the surfaces' immersed shares, each saturating on a flat plate (hi_alpha), derived 9.17 in pitch and 5.70 in yaw, the yaw over the same kick with the rudder centred (the right thrust and the swirl yaw it without one); 25 percent either way. A petrol engine idles rather than stopping: at its idle the wash's dp, and the authority, is (idle / hover rpm)^2 = 0.0978 of the hover's, under 1.5 times that

s11_harrier.source: level at a body angle of attack of 40 deg, the throttle holding height: the stalled wing's plate lift and the thrust's vertical share against the weight, derived 11.43 m/s at a stick of 0.319 with the elevator at 86 percent of its throw; the speed 20 percent and the throttle 15 percent either way, the elevator short of full

s12_knife_edge.source: rolled right to 90 deg at 30.76 m/s, height held on the rudder, the right thrust 3 deg down from the axis and its yaw on the rudder too: derived 25.4 deg of sideslip at a stick of 0.454 with the rudder at 100 percent of its throw; the sideslip 25 percent and the throttle 15 percent either way, the rudder short of full. Re-derived 2026-10-12 with the fuselage's crossflow on its drawn rounded box section, not a round body's: NACA TN 3038 Table I, the 1:2 ellipse 1.6 and the 1:1 rounded square at r/b 0.333 1.0 over the same tunnel's circle 1.0 (scripts/lib/crossflow.js), was 25.53 deg at 0.440; the same widths about it. Re-derived 2026-10-13 (w38-fuselage-side) with the fuselage's share of the weathercock, -0.0415 of 0.2270, on Munk's sin 2 beta (NACA TR 184, plant_wing.c MUNK'S MOMENT) where it was on sin beta: was 23.33 deg at 0.433, the rudder at 79 percent; the same widths about it. Re-derived 2026-10-13 (w38-crossflow-moment) with the fuselage's crossflow drag acting at its own centre of pressure, side_x ahead of the CG, Allen and Perkins' crossflow on the drawn sections (NACA TR 1048; plant_wing.c side_x, ESTIMATED), where it acted at the CG, -0.527 m: was 23.54 deg at 0.433, the rudder at 81 percent; the same widths about it. The derivation now needs 109 percent of the rudder's throw: no level knife edge at 30 m/s. Re-derived 2026-10-13 (w38-crossflow-moment): the derivation now flies the fin and rudder as the plant does (scripts/lib/knifefin.js) with Selig's jet normal force at the disc and the crossflow the disc turns (AIAA 2010-7938 eqs. 13 to 16, plant_wing.c jet_kj), which it had left out: was 27.01 deg at 0.445, the rudder at 109 percent; now 105 percent, still no level knife edge at 30 m/s; the same widths about it. Since 2026-10-13 (w38-crossflow-moment) the gate's hands are the knife edge's as taught (wingpilot.js knifeThrottle: Precision Aerobatics tip 8, power for altitude; Hawkinson, Model Aviation Sept 1999): the rudder put on to the derivation's share of its throw (rudderDerived) and left there, the height on the throttle alone (dutyDerived its trim), the speed where it falls; until then the hands held the gate's speed on the throttle, nobody's number, and the rudder flew the height. The derivation at the gate's speed predicts the sideslip and throttle the plant settles at; the same widths about it. Re-derived 2026-10-13 (w38-crossflow-moment): the derivation now flies the fin with the prop's swirl at it (knifefin.js xs: the torque on the air from the table's torque_curve at the thrust and speed flown, SWIRL_KEEP of it past the wing's root; Deters, Ananda and Selig 2015 fig. 22b; the one term npm run knife:budget found it lacked against the plant): the rudder was 105 percent of its throw, now 103, still no level knife edge at 30 m/s; the sideslip and throttle do not move; the same widths about it. The gate's speed, derived 2026-10-13 (w38-crossflow-moment; it was chosen, 30 m/s, with no source): the hardest level knife edge the derivation says the aircraft can hold, the speed at which the balance asks the most of the rudder among the speeds it asks no more than the full throw (scripts/slick-derive.js knifeGate; the rudder's share peaks between the slow side, where the fuselage's saturating side force gives way to the fin's weathercock, and the fast side, where the sideslip falls; on the Slick the peak is past the throw and this is the floor, the slowest speed with a level knife edge): 30.76 m/s, 25.42 deg of sideslip at 0.454 throttle with the rudder at 100 percent of its throw; the same widths about it. The rudder's clause is now the derivation's: its share within the throw.

s13_rest.source: the sheet's side view on its wheels, 9.38 deg nose up, the CG 0.4082 m up, 10.9 percent of the weight on the tailwheel; half a degree, 5 mm and 3.5 points either way

s14_takeoff.source: full throttle from standing, the engine spooling up from its idle on its map against the prop's torque curve, the tail up at 8 m/s and the nose to 8 deg at 15 m/s: liftoff at 15.8 m/s after 8.01 m (slick:derive); 40 percent short and 60 long, the Extra's, since the plant's roll has the gear's springs, the engine's spool and the pilot's hands in it and the derivation has none

s16_cross_host.source: the Slick's recorded take off, hover, torque roll and flight, state trace hash, Node against headless Chrome
